title: EFICAC-TTR Trial: Exercise and Nutritional Supplementation in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis
off: A Prospective, Randomized, Multicenter Clinical Trial on the Effect of a Home-Based Multicomponent Exercise Program Combined With Nutritional Supplementation in Patients With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis

officials.n: José A Pérez Rivera, PhD, MD

summary:
Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (TTR-CA) is a systemic cardiac disease that predominantly affects older adults and is frequently associated with reduced physical capacity, muscle weakness, frailty, and impaired quality of life. Although disease-modifying treatments can slow cardiac disease progression, functional and nutritional impairment remain important unmet clinical needs.

EFICAC-TTR is a prospective, randomized, multicenter study designed to evaluate the effects of a 12-week home-based multicomponent exercise program combined with nutritional supplementation in adults aged 70 years or older with confirmed TTR-CA.

A total of 47 participants were randomized to one of three parallel groups: (1) usual medical care; (2) a home-based multicomponent exercise program plus microcrystalline cellulose control supplementation; or (3) the same exercise program plus creatine monohydrate (3 g/day) and beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB, 3 g/day).

The primary functional outcomes are change in 6-minute walk test distance and handgrip strength from baseline to 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes include body composition, frailty, quality of life, and nutritional and clinical variables. Mechanistic biomarkers are assessed as exploratory outcomes.

The study aims to determine whether combining exercise with nutritional supplementation can improve functional capacity and related health outcomes in older adults with TTR-CA.
desc:
Participants were randomized to three parallel study groups. The usual-care group continued standard clinical management without a structured exercise program or study supplementation. Participants in the two exercise groups performed the same 12-week home-based multicomponent exercise program adapted to individual functional capacity.

In addition to exercise, one group received daily microcrystalline cellulose as a control supplement, whereas the experimental group received creatine monohydrate (3 g/day) plus beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB, 3 g/day). The supplement comparison was blinded, while the comparison with usual care was necessarily open because of the behavioral intervention. Functional outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks.

Biological samples collected at baseline and after the intervention are used for exploratory mechanistic analyses.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥70 years.
* Confirmed diagnosis of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (TTR-CA) based on positive bone scintigraphy with diphosphonates (Perugini grade 2 or 3) and absence of monoclonal protein.
* Clinical stability during the 4 weeks prior to enrollment.
* Ability to understand the study procedures and provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Light-chain (AL) amyloidosis or other non-TTR amyloidosis variants.
* Absolute medical contraindication to moderate-intensity exercise.
* Severe comorbid conditions with an estimated life expectancy \<6 months.
* Severe cognitive impairment (Mini-Mental State Examination score \<20).
* Concurrent participation in another clinical trial or structured exercise program.
* Known allergy or intolerance to creatine, beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB), or microcrystalline cellulose.
* Severe renal impairment requiring dialysis.

arms.d: Participants received usual medical care for transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, including routine cardiology follow-up and general lifestyle and nutritional recommendations, without the structured study exercise program or study supplementation.

Participants performed a 12-week home-based multicomponent exercise program and received daily microcrystalline cellulose as the control supplement. The supplement was provided in sachets matched to the supplementation procedure used in the experimental arm.
i: Dietary Supplement: Microcrystalline Cellulose Control Supplementation

arms.d: Participants performed the same 12-week home-based multicomponent exercise program and received daily supplementation with creatine monohydrate (3 g/day) and beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate (HMB, 3 g/day).
i: Dietary Supplement: Creatine and HMB Supplementation
